notes.observation: Kalaignar anticipates that some may call his Tamil feeling 'வெறி' and answers that if devotion/attachment ('பற்று') is called frenzy, then that meaning is correct.

notes.observation: The chapter repeatedly personifies and militarises language politics: Tamil Mother threatened by the dagger of compulsory Hindi, Tamil feeling in blood and breath, a language war in which the narrator says he sprouted, and Thalamuthu/Natarajan as 'தமிழ்க் காளையர்'.

secondary_witnesses.role: secondary page-level text witnesses used to recover page joins, paragraphing, dialogue and song lineation; not authority over the pinned autobiography source

external_contextual_evidence.finding: Historical accounts independently identify a 1938 Tamilar Padai/Tamil brigade march from Tiruchirappalli to Madras led by Pattukkottai Alagiri/Azhagirisamy with Moovalur Ramamirtham among its prominent participants. This corroborates event identity only; the memoir's wording and scale remain controlling.

A contemporary Justice newspaper report from November 1938 identifies N. V. Natarajan as Secretary of the Peddunaickenpet Tamilar Kazagam, supporting the identity and English initials behind the page-48/49 split name.

Historical summaries identify Stalin Jagadeesan's 1938 anti-Hindi fast and Periyar's opposition to fasting as a protest method. The memoir's green-stone-ring anecdote remains an authored reported anecdote and is not independently promoted to verified fact.
Tamil lexicon evidence records 'கல்' as a historical mile/distance unit; the chapter itself later restates the march distance using 'மைல்'.
